question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: NVIDIA's recent next-quarter guide midpoints vs. the just-reported actual. Q1 FY27 guide 78 on Q4 actual ~68.1 (1.145x; ~68.1 from memory), Q2 guide 91 on Q1 actual 81.6 (1.115x), Q3 guide 108 on Q2 actual 96.2 (1.123x). Recent beats vs guide midpoint were +4.6% (Q1) and +5.7% (Q2), implying a Q3 actual around 111-115B; thin Polymarket DC markets lean to ~111-112B. Central estimate 112 x ~1.12 = ~126B. Upside: 70% FY28 growth guide, Rubin full production, management flagged a stronger hyperscaler pickup in Q4. Downside: power/infrastructure constraints, conservative guiding, China excluded. Markets: no market on the Q4 guide; Polymarket 'Q3 Data Center revenue above $X' contracts are a near-miss (different quarter, DC segment only, actuals not guidance), ~$2.1k total volume and internally inconsistent (>105B 46c, >110B 49c on fetch; harness snapshot showed 28c for >105B) - weak evidence only, not an anchor.

- Aug 26, 2026 call: CFO guided ~70% FY2028 revenue growth, described as supply-constrained (Wall St had ~45%). Vera Rubin ~20% of DC revenue in Q3, in full production (CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure, OCI, Nebius).

- Status quo: NVIDIA guides +/-2% around a midpoint; the next guide is typically ~11-15% above the just-reported actual.
- Resolution: off the midpoint of the Q4 FY27 revenue range in the Q3 FY27 press release 'Outlook' section (expected ~Nov 18-19, 2026), rounded to the nearest $1B; not off actual Q3 revenue or consensus.
- Event window: guidance published in the Q3 FY27 release (late Nov 2026); as of Oct 21, 2026 not yet published (0% resolved).

calls.reasoning: Recent pattern: NVIDIA beats its own guide by ~5% (Q1 81.6 vs 78; Q2 96.2 vs 91), then guides the next quarter ~11.5-12.5% above the actual (91/81.6, 108/96.2). Q3 guided 108 -> actual ~113 -> Q4 guide ~127. Yahoo consensus for the Jan quarter is ~124.5B, and NVIDIA's Q3 guide came in ~4% above the consensus before the Q2 print (108 vs 104.2), which supports 126-130. Rubin is in full production, supply is constrained, and FY28 is guided to +70%, all supporting continued sequential growth. Downside: supply limits or conservatism; China excluded from the outlook. Markets: no human market on this contract; thin Polymarket Q3 data-center-revenue markets (<$1k volume, different quantity) imply DC ~100-108B, consistent with total Q3 ~109-115B, weak evidence only.

Nvidia has beaten the top of its guidance range for 12 straight quarters, so Q3 actual should be about $112-114B. Applying 1.12-1.15 gives about $126-130B. Yahoo's consensus for Q4 actual revenue is about $124.5B, and Nvidia's guides have run about 3-4% above consensus. Management says component supply caps growth at about 70%, which works against a very large step-up. Polymarket only has thin-volume Q3 Data Center revenue contracts, which do not match this question, so no market anchor.

calls.reasoning: NVIDIA beat its guide by ~5% in the last two quarters, so Q3 actual ~112-114B vs the 108B guide. Next-quarter guides have run 1.115-1.145x the just-reported actual -> ~126-130B. Yahoo Q4 consensus is ~124.5B and NVIDIA's guides have recently topped pre-print consensus by ~4%, consistent with ~127-129B. Guide-to-guide steps (+13, +13, +17B) also point to ~125-128B. Supply constraints (management says demand is ~2x what 70% FY28 growth allows) and China exclusion temper the upside. Median 127B.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same evidence (guide history, ~5% beats, 1.12-1.15 ratio, ~124.5B Q4 consensus, supply-constrained Rubin ramp) and land at medians of 126-127. Q4 FY26 actual ~68.1B was unverified in Run 1 but asserted by Runs 2 and 3, so I accepted it. The Q4 consensus of ~124.5B (Yahoo) is cited in two runs and contradicted by none. The remaining disagreement is the dispersion width (7.7 vs 9 vs 13). I built mine from its components: ~9B. I chose a median of 127 because the guide-to-guide acceleration and the guide-over-consensus pattern both support it, with supply caps limiting the upside. No market matches the contract; the Polymarket Q3 DC-revenue contracts are a thin near-miss and not an anchor. The criteria text's 'Aug 26' date is evidently a template carryover; the release is expected ~Nov 17-18, 2026.
